valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 15 Nov 2026. (1) Business: one business, the PickMe app, earning platform fees on rides and deliveries; a software platform whose demand is transport, so weighted half internet software, half transportation. (2) Damodaran's emerging-markets dataset (betaEmerg) could NOT be opened: his site is blocked by this run's network settings. Stand-ins from web-search extracts of his tables: Software (Internet) global unlevered, cash-corrected 1.34 (date not shown in the extract); Transportation US unlevered 0.71 (January 2026). 0.5 × 1.34 + 0.5 × 0.71 = 1.03. (3) Net cash (Rs 3.7bn at Sep 2026, against market value Rs 57bn), so debt to equity 0 and no relevering: 1.03. (4) Local 5-year betas: none exist; the share listed on 3 October 2024, so there are only about two years of prices. TradingView shows 1-year betas of 0.51 and 0.65 (ignored, as the brief says). (5) Higher of 1.03 and (no local figure) = 1.03. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7) Into the formula by scripts/reinvestment.py. Provisional: refresh in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets file, and use local 5-year betas once October 2029 gives five years of trading.

valuationInputs.name: Cost of equity
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (21 Nov 2026): 8.24% + 1.03 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 18.8%, ±1.5 points. Unchanged from 15 Nov.

valuationInputs.name: WACC
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (21 Nov 2026): net cash Rs 1.40bn (Rs 0.32bn leases less Rs 1.72bn cash and bank, 30 Sep 2026; the Rs 2.28bn fixed deposits are valued separately) against market value Rs 58.75bn at Rs 176, so debt weight 0% and WACC = cost of equity. Lease cost of debt 13.66% (interest Rs 46.5mn ÷ average leases, FY 2026) carries no weight.

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 12% / 18% / 24% for seven years; supported 5.8% (reinvestment rate 5.0% × return on capital 116.3%, FY 2026). All three above by 6–18 pts.
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py on the FY 2026 figures rebuilt on 21 Nov 2026 (was −0.4% on the 15 Nov figures, which counted right-of-use amortisation in depreciation). Kept because the growth is already being delivered without capital: revenue +49% in FY 2026 and +38% in H1 FY2027 (Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 4) while reinvestment was Rs 0.11bn; most growth costs (driver and rider incentives, marketing, most engineering pay) run through profit, drivers own the vehicles and driver payables fund working capital. Profit kept × ROE gives 24.0%, above all three, and the DCF still charges growth ÷ 40 / 60 / 80% return on capital as reinvestment every year (18% ÷ 60% = 30% of profit in the base case, six times what FY 2026 needed).

valuationInputs.name: Growth
valuationInputs.value: Bear 12% then 5% / Base 18% then 6% / Bull 24% then 7%
valuationInputs.reason: Seven years, then long-run. Revenue +38% and profit +49% in H1 FY2027 (Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 4), +49% and +88% in FY 2026; growth should slow as the app matures. Long-run below the 12.24% bond and WACC.

valuationInputs.name: Long-term growth
valuationInputs.reason: The long-run figures of the Growth entry, used the same way in the DCF, P/E and dividend model; below the 12.24% bond yield and WACC.

valuationInputs.name: Return on new capital
valuationInputs.reason: Return on capital 116% in FY 2026 on opening capital (scripts/reinvestment.py); set far lower so the DCF charges real reinvestment as the business matures. From 21 Nov 2026 the return after the growth years is lowered to 25 / 30 / 35% (Damodaran moves stable-period ROC towards the cost of capital; kept above WACC because the platform needs little capital), so long-run growth needs 20% of profit reinvested.

valuationInputs.name: After-tax operating profit (start)
valuationInputs.value: Bear FY 2026 / Base twelve months to Sep 2026 / Bull Sep 2026 quarter × 4 (calculated)
valuationInputs.reason: Operating profit Rs 3.05bn (FY 2026), Rs 3.62bn (twelve months to Sep 2026) and Rs 4.17bn (Sep 2026 quarter × 4, Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 4), after the FY 2026 effective tax rate of 30.9%. Finance income on deposits is excluded (deposits are added separately). Replaces the hand-set Rs 2.4 / 2.5 / 2.6bn.

valuationInputs.name: Cash after maintenance capex (start)
valuationInputs.value: Bear after-tax operating profit + FY 2026 depreciation − maintenance / Base FY 2026 operating cash − maintenance / Bull twelve-month operating cash − maintenance (calculated)
valuationInputs.reason: Bear leaves out working capital and non-cash provisions (Rs 2.11bn + 0.69bn − 0.89bn = Rs 1.91bn); base is the calculator's FY 2026 figure (operating cash Rs 3.41bn, lease interest in financing so nothing added back, less Rs 0.69bn = Rs 2.73bn); bull the twelve months to Sep 2026 (Rs 3.87bn − 0.69bn = Rs 3.18bn). Operating cash runs above profit partly because payables to drivers rise with volume and tax is paid after it is charged. Replaces the hand-set Rs 2.5 / 2.8 / 3.0bn.

valuationInputs.name: Maintenance capex basis
valuationInputs.reason: No company split. Depreciation of PPE plus amortisation of own software (Rs 0.109bn + 0.580bn, FY 2026); right-of-use amortisation left out because leases are counted as debt. Bear = average capex booked FY 2025–26 (Rs 0.82bn and 0.96bn). Software amortisation is a real cost of keeping the platform current, so it isn't taken off.

valuationInputs.name: Fixed deposits (add-on)
valuationInputs.value: Fixed deposits at book, per share (Rs 6.83 at 30 Sep 2026)
valuationInputs.reason: Other investments (fixed deposits) Rs 2,281mn (Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 6) ÷ 333.8mn shares; the 1000 converts Rs bn to Rs a share. Added to the DCF in every case; the cash and money-market balance (Rs 1.72bn) is in net debt. Part of the cash pile is matched by Rs 1.23bn of payables, mostly to drivers.

valuationInputs.name: R&D life
valuationInputs.reason: Development is already capitalised under LKAS 38 (Rs 0.81bn in FY 2026, 4-year life); research expensed isn't disclosed, so no adjustment and no double counting.

valuationInputs.name: ROE path
valuationInputs.reason: ROE (on average equity) 70.6% for the twelve months to Sep 2026 (derived.py), company figures 49% FY 2024, 54% FY 2025, 68.7% FY 2026 (Annual Report 2025/26, pp. 10, 14); fades as cash builds and competition matures. The long-run figure sets the payout in the justified P/E and the dividend model (1 − growth ÷ ROE = 80% / 80% / 80%).

valuationInputs.name: EPS to March 2027 × P/E
valuationInputs.reason: H1 EPS Rs 4.24 (Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 4); second half 20% / 35% / 45% above last year's Rs 3.76 (FY 2026 Rs 6.61 less H1 FY2026 Rs 2.85). Base 0.9% below the Rs 9.40 run-rate (Sep quarter × 4), bear 6.9% below. From 21 Nov 2026 the P/E is the stable-growth justified P/E from scripts/valuation.py, (1 − g ÷ ROE) ÷ (cost of equity − g) at 5 / 6 / 7% growth (5.2× / 6.3× / 7.8×), in line with the 5.8% growth reinvestment supports; it replaces the hand-worked two-stage P/E of 6.5× / 9.4× / 14.7×, whose growth premium is already in the DCF and the dividend model.

valuationInputs.name: Dividend this year
valuationInputs.reason: 65% payout of the EPS estimate (the payout behind the Rs 2.75 interim for 2026/27, Interim to 30 Sep 2026, p. 3); growing with profit for seven years, then the long-run payout 1 − growth ÷ ROE.

valuationInputs.name: Methods used
valuationInputs.value: Whole-company DCF + fixed deposits, stable justified P/E, two-stage dividend model
valuationInputs.reason: Asset-light cash generator; NAV, P/B and residual income not useful with such a small book value (Rs 13.34 against EPS Rs 8).

openQuestions: Q3 results (to December 2026, due by mid-February): does profit growth stay above 35%, and does the September quarter's 36% operating margin hold?
Beta: refresh in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets file (Software (Internet), Transportation); the current 1.03 is a stand-in.
Capitalised software development: does it keep pace with revenue (Rs 0.43bn in H1 FY2027 against Rs 0.38bn)? Any write-off?
Tax and VAT assessments under appeal: contingent liabilities Rs 837mn (income tax) and Rs 1.66bn (VAT) at March 2026 (note 23). Any ruling against the company?
Do fuel supply problems come back and hit driver numbers (they cut trips in the June 2026 quarter)?
Price competition: does the 10.3% take rate hold?
What happens to the Rs 4bn of cash and deposits: higher dividends, new verticals, or acquisitions?
Can the 2021/22 operating loss be confirmed with a figure (the 2025/26 annual report shows it only in a chart, p. 42)?

changeLog.basedOn: Annual Report 2025/26 and interims to 30 Jun and 30 Sep 2026 (CSE downloads), re-read in full
changeLog.summary: Requested from Telegram (/redo PKME full). Research record rebuilt from the downloaded reports: FY 2026 and FY 2025 reinvestment figures added (capex booked 0.96 / 0.82, of which own software development 0.81 / 0.68; depreciation and amortisation 0.80 / 0.61; working capital −0.16 / −0.03; no acquisitions; operating profit 3.05 / 1.60; tax 30.9% / 30.5%; equity; leases, cash and deposits, no borrowings; interest paid 0.047 / 0.042, financing section; dividends paid), H1 FY2027 cash flow, capex and net cash, a Q2 FY2027 quarter and a trailing-12-month period. Earlier figures, reportsRead and change log kept. Beta 1.03 (provisional: Damodaran's site was blocked, so global/US sector betas from web-search extracts; no local 5-year beta exists as the share listed in October 2024) gives cost of equity 18.8% (was 16% by hand); WACC the same (net cash). Capex-based supported growth −0.4% (asset-light, negative working capital); growth 12 / 18 / 24% kept with reasons, profit kept × ROE 24%. DCF now whole-company at WACC plus net cash: weighted 146.8 → 116.0; P/E now a justified P/E 144.5 → 89.2; dividend model 101.3 → 86.4. R&D already capitalised, no adjustment. Business tests re-scored 4 → 3 of 4: steady profit now fails (operating loss in 2021/22 shown in the annual report's chart, p. 42; no figure given). Still 'good'; category unchanged (watch list). Fair value Rs 131.0 → 97.2, buy Rs 111.4 → 82.6, strong buy Rs 98.3 → 72.9. No report problems.

Requested from Telegram (/redo PKME.N0000 full). Rebuilt the record from the CSE copies of the 2025/26 annual report and the June and September 2026 interims: printed figures only, comparative columns as their own periods (FY 2025, Q1, Q2 and H1 FY2026), the worked-out twelve-month period, net debt and tax rates removed, purchase lines and fixed deposits split out, right-of-use amortisation left out of depreciation. All three methods now come from scripts/valuation.py (modelInputs added); the code reproduces the old hand-worked DCF and dividend model exactly with the old inputs. Changes: the P/E method uses the stable-growth justified P/E (was a hand-worked two-stage P/E), DCF start cash and profit now derived from recorded figures (were set by hand), return on capital after the growth years 25/30/35%, deposits valued as an add-on. Added management and shareholders sections. Beta 1.03 and cost of equity 18.8% unchanged. Business tests still 3/4 (steady-profit fails on the 2021/22 operating loss): good, watch list. Fair value Rs 97.20 → Rs 83.25.
